title: The Playlist of Westbrook High
premise: Tamsin Villalobos, a scholarship student at Westbrook Academy, is surviving on coffee, financial aid paperwork, and the fragile friendship of her study group — until an anonymous group chat called The Playlist starts sending them song titles that predict school events days before they happen. When a predicted 'accident' nearly kills a classmate, Tamsin realizes the playlist isn't prophecy; it's a warning system built by someone who knows what the school board buried: a hazing scandal covered up years ago that ruined a scholarship kid just like her. Racing the last football game of the season, Tamsin and her friends trace the chat to its source and expose the board's cover-up at the homecoming broadcast — but only after Tamsin must choose between protecting her own future at Westbrook and doing justice for a student the school erased.
about_author: Elodie Nystrom is a former debate coach who spent six years teaching at elite private schools before turning to fiction full-time. She writes stories about sharp-tongued outsiders who refuse to be grateful for crumbs.

chapters.title: Fine Is a Four-Letter Word
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. We meet Westbrook through her eyes: the marble lobby she's not allowed to touch, the scholarship kids' unofficial lunch table in the stairwell, and her study group — Priya, Marcus, and quiet new transfer Dev. Establishes her precarity and pride. Emotional beat: defiant loneliness disguised as competence.

chapters.title: Track One
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. An unknown number adds all four of them to a group chat called The Playlist. First message: a song title, 'The Fire This Time,' with a date three days out. They laugh it off — until the chemistry lab fire drill happens exactly then, down to the minute. Beat: unease creeping under sarcasm.

chapters.title: The Stairwell Society
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. The group argues about whether to leave the chat; Priya secretly wants to stay because being chosen feels like belonging. A second prediction lands: a locker number and the word 'confess.' Beat: the intoxicating, dangerous pull of being seen.

chapters.title: Locker 214
chapters.summary: Marcus's POV. They stake out locker 214 and find it belongs to Owen Reyes, a popular senior whose brother attended Westbrook years ago on scholarship. Inside: old newspaper clippings about a hazing incident the school calls 'the winter of the misunderstanding.' Beat: first real fear.

chapters.title: Everything Is Fine (A Recurring Motif)
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Headmaster Whitlock convenes an assembly about 'digital harassment,' clearly spooked. Tamsin notices him watching her specifically — the scholarship kid with the loudest mouth. She lies smoothly to his face and hates how good she's gotten at it. Beat: corruption begins at the top.

chapters.title: The Boy Who Was Here
chapters.summary: Dev's POV. Dev reveals he transferred because of rumors about Westbrook, and he's been digging: in 2016, scholarship student Mateo Reyes was expelled after a hazing injury left him hospitalized — the school blamed him. Owen is his younger brother. Beat: grief and righteous anger.

chapters.title: Interlude: Someone Is Typing
chapters.summary: Group chat transcript chapter, all POVs braided. The Playlist goes silent for two days, then sends one message: 'They buried him under a full ride. Ask who paid for yours.' Every member suspects every other member of being the anonymous admin. Beat: trust fracturing.

chapters.title: Full Ride
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Tamsin investigates her own scholarship and finds its funding flows through a foundation controlled by board chair Richard Hale — the same man who signed Mateo's expulsion. The Playlist knew. She realizes she's not just a member; she might be a message. Beat: betrayal and vertigo.

chapters.title: Homecoming Is a Weapon
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. The school announces the homecoming game will stream live, celebrating Westbrook's centennial. Priya maps the power structure: Whitlock, Hale, the alumni network. If they're going to expose anything, the broadcast is the only stage big enough. Beat: strategy replacing panic.

chapters.title: The Archive Room Smells Like Vindication
chapters.summary: Marcus's POV. Marcus, the school's AV volunteer, gets them into the archive. They find the incident report from 2016 — redacted, but with a witness list. One name is still on staff: Coach Brennan, now beloved, now coaching the centennial game. Beat: the past has a face.

chapters.title: Coach Brennan's Good Year
chapters.summary: Dev's POV. They approach Brennan cautiously; he deflects, then privately admits he was pressured to stay silent — but refuses to go on record, terrified for his family. Dev rages at another adult choosing safety over truth. Beat: complicity wears a friendly face.

chapters.title: Predictions End
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. The Playlist sends its final scheduled track — and it predicts something catastrophic: 'Last song. Last game. He falls again.' Aimed at Owen, who has been asking questions publicly. Now it's not about exposure; someone may get hurt. Beat: dread crystallizing into resolve.

chapters.title: Suspects in a Group Chat
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. The four turn on each other, running alibis. Priya catches Dev deleting messages and confronts him; he confesses he contacted Mateo Reyes directly weeks ago — and Mateo told him to stop, that Westbrook destroys people who dig. Beat: the cost of loyalty tested.

chapters.title: Mateo
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Against everyone's wishes, Tamsin finds Mateo working nights across town. Broken, bitter, he tells her the truth of 2016 — and warns her that Hale will ruin her the way he ruined him, and no one will stop him. But he gives her one thing: the unredacted report he kept. Beat: inherited wounds, passed torch.

chapters.title: The Offer
chapters.summary: Marcus's POV. Whitlock summons Tamsin and offers her a full-ride renewal, a glowing recommendation, anything — if she hands over the documents and distances herself from the others. Marcus watches her almost take it. Beat: temptation made generous, corruption made polite.

chapters.title: What Gratitude Costs
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Tamsin tells the group about the offer and, worse, that she considered it. Priya explodes; Dev goes cold; Marcus defends her. The group shatters two days before the game. Alone, Tamsin reads Mateo's report and understands the Playlist's purpose completely. Beat: rock bottom, clarity rising.

chapters.title: The Admin
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Reassembling the clues, Priya identifies the Playlist's admin: Ms. Okafor, the school nurse who treated Mateo in 2016 and has been quietly documenting ever since. Okafor doesn't deny it — she says she needed students the board couldn't predict. Beat: allies hiding in plain sight.

chapters.title: Setlist
chapters.summary: All four POVs interwoven. The plan: during the centennial broadcast, swap the tribute video with the unredacted report, witness statements, and hospital records. Each takes a role — Marcus on AV, Priya on timing, Dev on Brennan's statement, Tamsin as decoy at the board's VIP box. Beat: fear transmuted into purpose.

chapters.title: Last Game of the Season
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Game night. Stadium lights, centennial banners, Hale shaking hands. Tamsin stalls the board members with charm while the feed switches — and the screen fills with Mateo's name, the redactions lifted, Brennan walking onto the field mid-broadcast to speak. Beat: breathless triumph with a countdown clock.

chapters.title: He Falls Again
chapters.summary: Dev's POV. The prediction comes true: Owen, confronting Hale in the stands, is shoved down the stairs — caught by Dev and classmates, injured but alive. Phones everywhere capture everything, including Hale's face. The cover-up attempt becomes the confession. Beat: terror flipping to undeniable proof.

chapters.title: Aftermath, Unredacted
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. State investigators arrive; Whitlock resigns; Hale is indicted; Westbrook announces the Mateo Reyes Scholarship. Mateo attends the board's public apology and doesn't forgive them — he just nods at Tamsin. Okafor retires, leaving the Playlist archived. Beat: justice without absolution.

chapters.title: Encore
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Weeks later, Tamsin keeps her scholarship — on her own terms, having refused Hale's tainted version. The stairwell table is bigger now; new scholarship kids sit there. Her phone buzzes: an unknown number, a single song title, a date. She smiles, and this time she answers. Beat: belonging earned, vigilance kept.
